naslov: "Did You Think That We Created You in Vain, and That You Would Not Be Returned to Us?"

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ يُحِقُّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلُ الْبَاطِلَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Who establishes the truth and abolishes falsehood, even if the criminals dislike it (cf. Al-Anfal 8:8).

segmenti.tekst: وَنَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَنَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَحَبِيبُهُ وَصَفِيُّهُ وَخَلِيلُهُ أَدَّى الْأَمَانَةَ وَبَلَّغَ الرِّسَالَةَ وَنَصَحَ الْأُمَّةَ وَجَاهَدَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِ حَتَّى أَتَاهُ الْيَقِينُ
segmenti.prevod: We bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and we bear witness that Muhammad is His servant, His beloved, His chosen one and His close friend. He fulfilled the trust, conveyed the message, gave sincere counsel to the ummah and strove in the way of Allah as He deserves, until certainty (death) came to him.

segmenti.tekst: وَتَرَكَنَا عَلَى الْمَحَجَّةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ لَيْلُهَا كَنَهَارِهَا لَا يَزِيغُ عَنْهَا بَعْدَهُ إِلَّا هَالِكٌ
segmenti.prevod: He left us upon the clear white path whose night is like its day; none strays from it after him except one who is ruined.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah the Exalted says in His noble Book: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: All glory and praise belong to Allah, jalla sha'nuhu (exalted is His majesty), the Lord of all creation, the Lord of the known and the unknown, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of the noble Throne. May sincere blessings and peace be upon Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), the best man who ever walked the face of the earth, the best of all the prophets and messengers. May sincere blessings and peace be upon him, upon his honourable, esteemed and respected family, upon his virtuous companions, and upon all those who follow the path of Islam, the path of the Qur'an, the path of salvation, until the Day of Judgement. Allahumma amin.

Esteemed brothers and respected believers, everything that Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, has created, He has created for a reason, He has created with a purpose. There is absolutely nothing that He, the Exalted, the Absolutely Wise, has created without that created thing having a reason for which it was created and its own function.

So if we look at the hills, the seas, the oceans, the mountains and so on, we will see that every created thing has its function and a great wisdom for which the Exalted Lord created it. And He, the Exalted, the Absolutely Wise, created everything He created in this world, brothers, for our sake.

Allah has subjected to man everything that is on the Earth. And what has been subjected to us, brothers, we must use for positive things and constructive purposes. And life in this world is very short, very short. However long a person lives in this world, brothers, he will surely return to his Lord.

And Allah informs us in Surah Al-Mu'minun and says that He will ask people on the Day of Judgement – especially the unbelievers, but He will also ask the believers: "How long did you spend in the world?"
What will they say? "Our Lord, we were in the world a day or part of a day. Ask those who kept count." What will Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, say?

"Truly, you lived in the world only a short while, if only you had known!" And we see, brothers, that the people of Jahannam (Hellfire) will say that they lived in the world a day or part of a day. And what does Allah say? He says: "Truly, you lived in the world only a little, you lived a very short time.

If only you had been aware of that." If only you had known it, and had used that short life the way it should be used. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: when the people of Jannah (Paradise) have entered Jannah, and the people of Jahannam have entered Jahannam, Allah will address the people of Jannah and say: "O people of Jannah, how long did you live in the world?" And they will say: "A day or part of a day, our Lord."

What will Allah say to them? "How wonderful your trade was! For one day, or part of a day, you have earned My mercy, My pleasure and Jannah." Then Allah will ask the people of Jahannam, the inhabitants of Jahannam: "Kam labithtum fil-ard?" – how long did you spend in the world?

And they, brothers, will answer the same way as the people of Jannah answered. They will say: "Our Lord, we stayed in the world a day or part of a day." And to those words Allah will say: "How ugly your trade was, how bad your trade was! For that one day, or part of a day, you have earned My wrath, My wrath, and you have deserved the Fire; so remain in Jahannam, in it you will abide forever."

Then Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, says: "O people, did you think that We created you in vain?" Did you think that We created you just like that, merely to be created, that you have no mission and no role in this world,
وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا تُرْجَعُونَ
segmenti.prevod: “…and that you would not be returned to Us?” (Al-Mu'minun 23:115)

segmenti.tekst: "and that you would not be returned to Us?" What is Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, saying here, brothers? Allah is sending us a message: O My servants – here Allah addresses all of mankind and says – O My servants, do you think that you will not return to your Lord? Live freely as long as you like, do what you like, but know that one day you will surely return to the Lord.

And in the previous ayah Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, says: truly, you were in this world only a little while, and it would have been better for you to have made use of this life. And life in this world, brothers, is one chance, one opportunity that Allah gives each of us.

No one in this world, brothers, has two chances. It is like an exam that has only one sitting. Not like exams at our universities or universities around the world, where we have a great many sittings, so if we do not pass one sitting we have another, and if we do not pass the second we have a third, and so on.

Life in this world, brothers, is an exam that has only one sitting. And from the time of our physical maturity we are writing, taking that exam. And according to our answers, our deeds, both verbal and physical, our result will be, or that will be our grade.

And we have the opportunity for that test until the angel of death comes. And the angel of death will surely come to each of us. When he will come, we do not know. None of us, brothers, has it written down, so that he personally knows, when the angel of death will come to him. It is written with the Lord, Allah knows, but we do not know when the angel of death will come to us.

And until then, until that hour, we all have the opportunity to improve ourselves. And we all need to be better, to be better Muslims, better believers, and so on. And many people, brothers, will regret not having made use of the life that Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, gave them. Many will regret not having made use of that one chance, that day, brothers, or part of a day, as Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, says in the Qur'an.

And Allah tells us about a category of people with whom He, the Exalted, is not pleased, and He says: when the angel of death comes to one of them, he has only one wish, one request of the Lord of all the worlds.

And that request is the following: "My Lord, give me just one more chance. My Lord, give me just one more opportunity." Why? Why, brothers, does he ask for one more chance? What is his vision, what would he want to put right in his life if Allah gave him one more chance?

What would he do with that chance which you and I have today? He says: "La'alli a'malu salihan fima taraktu" – "My Lord, give me one more chance, so that I may do good deeds. Just one more chance, even if only to do one more good deed." What will the Lord of the worlds say to him?
"By no means." There is no chance. It will be nothing but a mere wish, a mere spoken word.
وَمِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
segmenti.prevod: “…and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.” (Al-Mu'minun 23:100)

segmenti.tekst: And the people who have passed away will remain in their graves, brothers, "ila yawmi yub'athun" – until the Day of Judgement. And imagine how many generations have passed away! How many generations, brothers, are in the grave? How many people are in the graves? And every person, every individual, will remain in his grave "ila yawmi yub'athun" – until the Day of Resurrection.

And Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, will then resurrect all of mankind, and He says: "Fa idha nufikha fis-suri" – and when the Horn is blown – "fala ansaba baynahum yawma'idhin wa la yatasa'alun" – on that day the ties of kinship are severed. Brothers, the ties of kinship are severed on the Day of Judgement.

We know how much we love our parents. We know how much we love our children. We know how much someone means to us in life – we would give everything in this world. But in the world to come, Allah says, there will be no ties of kinship. A child may come to his mother – and we know how much mothers, parents love their children – and say to the parent: "Father, or mother, give me just one good deed; I need just one good deed to tip the scale, so that, that is, my good deeds are over 50%," and the father or mother will say to him: "My son, my little son, I do not know what my final outcome will be, I do not know what will become of me; perhaps I will need that one good deed myself."

And Allah says in Surah 'Abasa: "Yawma yafirrul-mar'u min akhihi" – the day – this refers to the Day of Judgement – when, He says, "yawma yafirrul-mar'u min akhihi" – when a man will flee from his brother – "wa ummihi wa abihi" – and from his mother and his father – "wa sahibatihi wa banih" – and from his wife and his children.

On that day every person will be preoccupied with himself. Every person, brothers, will be thinking about himself. And Allah says: "فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ" – in the next ayah – and as for him whose scale of good deeds is heavy, whoever has many good deeds.

What does it mean, brothers, whose scale of good deeds is heavy? The best-known commentator of the Qur'an among the companions of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, Abdullah ibn Abbas, says: the scale of good deeds, or the scale that is heavy – and as for him whose scale of good deeds is heavy – he says, this refers to those who have even one good deed over 50%.

That is, even one deed, so that even slightly that good deed, or that positive energy, tips the balance. So, He says, those whose scale of good deeds is heavy will be the greatest winners. That, brothers, is the greatest success. The greatest success, brothers, that a person can achieve is that his scale of good deeds is heavy on the Day of Judgement,

that Allah is pleased with him. That, brothers, is the greatest success. Worldly successes are also very important for a Muslim – Muslims must be good in every sense and in every field – but the greatest success, brothers, the greatest triumph, is that Allah is pleased with us and that our scale of good deeds is heavy on the Day of Judgement.

Then Allah says in the next ayah: "Wa man khaffat mawazinuhu" – and as for him whose scale of good deeds is light, that is, whoever did few good deeds, whoever was not diligent in that field – "fa ula'ikal-ladhina khasiru anfusahum" – those are the ones who have ruined themselves, who destroyed themselves with their own hands, and they will be in the Fire forever. We have, brothers, an opportunity. We have an opportunity – how long we will have that opportunity, we do not know.

But for that reason we should strive and we should ask Allah. And that is in fact what we do in every rak'ah we pray: in absolutely every rak'ah we recite the ayah "Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim" – guide us, our Lord, to the straight path. And that, brothers, is a very important, very significant supplication.

If that supplication were not so important, Allah would not have prescribed it, or that ayah would not be in every rak'ah for us to recite. And in every rak'ah we recite: "Our Lord, guide us to the straight path" – "Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim." Why, brothers, to the straight path? Because there are a great many paths.

There are, brothers, a great many paths in this world, and Shaytan lies in wait on every one of those paths. But there is one straight path, and every other path besides the straight path is error. Every path besides the straight path is error. And that is why we constantly supplicate: "Our Lord, guide all Muslims to the straight path."

"Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have shown them the straight path, after You have guided them." And I ask Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, to have mercy on us, to let us see the truth as truth and follow it, and to see falsehood as falsehood and avoid it.

I ask Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, to make easy for us [unclear] and good deeds and everything of words and deeds with which Allah, jalla sha'nuhu, is pleased. I ask Him, the Exalted, to make it easy for us to abandon sinning and every deed or word with which the Exalted Lord is not pleased. And a supplication that the Prophet, alayhis-salam, recited very often was, or went like this: "My Lord, nothing is easy except what You make easy." So we ask You, our Lord, to make every khayr, every good, easy for us on this blessed day and at this blessed hour.
وَأَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: And I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
